messages.author: 87e020c3fd9325fa
messages.subject: Multinomial data with covariates
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to model population age structure as a multinomial variable based on the example provided in the FAQ.   I have been able to apply the example model to simple population age structure data with good results - ie the predicted age distribution closely matches the observed values. However, I am uncertain how to build a model that includes covariates.  

If I include covariates as a fixed effect in the formula, it is unclear to me what effect this should have on the Multinomial distribution as as whole. I would expect that it would have no effect on the Multinomial distribution.

If, however, I include a covariate as a weight (as suggested in the FAQ example), the predicted Multinomial distribution is very different to the data.  It looks to me as though including a covariate in this way does result in a Multinomial regression - type model in which we can estimate coefficients for each of the classes in the MND.

Can anyone point me to an example of how to implement a multinomial logistic regression in a way that allows estimation of coefficients for covariates (and thus prediction into unsampled data points)?

Many thanks,

Tom Bird

messages.author: 87e020c3fd9325fa
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Multinomial data with covariates
parts:
After some back and forth, it turns out that the solution is simply to use dummy variables to create new copies of the covariates for each class in the multinomial, setting the value to 0 where appropriate. Note that this requires the use of centred covariates.

R code attached provides an example

TB
